recognize_zh: 低倍骨髓切片中骨小樑之間幾乎全被大量粉紅細胞質的巨核細胞群佔據，左側可見細胞核呈流線狀排列（纖維化），脂肪與正常造血幾乎消失，於唐氏症兒童符合 ML-DS。
features: Hypercellular marrow with near-total replacement of intertrabecular spaces
Tremendous megakaryocytic hyperplasia with numerous megakaryocytes of variable size and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm
Streaming, spindled nuclei in the left fragment consistent with marrow fibrosis
Absence of marrow fat; residual normal hematopoiesis inconspicuous
describe_en: Low-power view of the bone marrow core biopsy shows a markedly hypercellular marrow with loss of fat. The intertrabecular spaces are replaced by a dense proliferation of megakaryocytes with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm and variably sized nuclei, admixed with smaller immature cells. In the left portion of the biopsy the nuclei are spindled and streaming, suggestive of reticulin fibrosis. In a child with Down syndrome, findings are consistent with myeloid leukemia associated with Down syndrome; reticulin stain and CD61/CD42b immunostains are recommended.

ddx.vs: PMF occurs in older adults with bizarre hyperchromatic cloud-like megakaryocytes and osteosclerosis, not sheets of megakaryoblasts in a Down syndrome child.

ddx.dx: Metastatic small round blue cell tumor with fibrosis
ddx.vs: Tumor cells form cohesive nests and lack platelet glycoprotein expression, while here the proliferation is megakaryocytic.
TAM occurs in neonates (usually <3 months) and resolves spontaneously, whereas ML-DS arises later (typically <5 years) often after a myelodysplastic phase with marrow fibrosis.
